Figure caption: (a) Schematic illustration of the targeted in vivo CAR-T cell therapy strategy using anti-hCD8 VHH-functionalized LNPs. For functionalization, VHH was genetically introduced with the LPXTG motif and converted to the S-acetyl group via a sortase A-mediated site-specific transpeptidation reaction, followed by deprotection of the acetyl group to yield VHH-SH. mRNA-LNPs including maleimide-PEG-DSPE were conjugated with VHH-SH via thiol–maleimide chemistry. CD8-targeted LNPs deliver CAR mRNA to T cells in vivo, leading to CAR expression and CD19+ cell killing. (b) SDS-PAGE/Western blotting confirmed VHH conjugation and purification by mobility shift. VHH alone was loaded as a control. (c) The mean hydrodynamic diameter of LNPs was measured by dynamic light scattering before and after VHH conjugation. (d) Schematic overview of the in vivo study in human PBMC-engrafted NSG mice following intravenous injection of FLuc or mCherry mRNA-loaded LNPs. (e) Representative bioluminescence images of each organ 6 h after LNP administration at 0.1 mg/kg mRNA. (f) Quantification of FLuc luminescence in each organ based on region-of-interest analysis. The color bar indicates radiance (p/sec/cm2/sr). Data are presented as the mean ± s.d., n = 4. (g) Relative expression percentage of FLuc signal by organ, showing preferential accumulation in the spleen. (h) Representative flow cytometry plots showing mCherry expression in human splenocytes 24 h after LNP administration at a dose of 0.4 mg/kg mRNA. Numbers in the quadrant gates represent the percentage of cells in each population. (i) Quantification of mCherry+ cells in human CD8+ T cells, CD4+ T cells, CD19+ B cells, and Tregs. With hCD8-VHH decoration on LNPs, reporter expression was highest in CD8+ T cells with minimal off-target transfection. Data are presented as the mean ± s.d., n = 3. Statistical significance was evaluated using two-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s posthoc test (i) to compare mCherry expression across treatment groups and cell types, and one-way ANOVA (f) for organ-wise luminescence comparisons versus the unconjugated LNP group (*P ≤ 0.05, ***P ≤ 0.001, ****P ≤ 0.0001; ns = not significant, P > 0.05).

Figure caption: (a) Experimental design for engineering LNPs with tunable surface VHH densities. Anti-hCD8 VHHs were site-specifically conjugated to maleimide-functionalized LNPs at input molar ratios ranging from 0.008 to 0.5 mol %. (b) Hydrodynamic diameter of all VHH-LNP formulations, measured by dynamic light scattering. (c) SDS-PAGE/Western blotting analysis of purified LNPs showing increasing band intensity corresponding to input VHH levels. (d) Total protein quantification of purified LNPs (20 μg mRNA/mL) by the BCA assay also showed dose-dependent increases. (e) Schematic of the nanoflow cytometry-based workflow to quantify functionally accessible surface VHH. (f) Co-elution of DiR and AF488 signals confirmed successful probe binding to LNPs. Crucially, free AF488–hCD8 was well separated from the LNP fractions, enabling clean downstream analysis. (g) Representative nanoFCM raw trace showing simultaneous detection of side scatter and AF488 fluorescence as discrete peaks over time, demonstrating single-particle codetection. (h) Calibration with size and MESF (molecules of equivalent soluble fluorophore) bead standards enabled the conversion of scatter and fluorescence signals to particle diameter and number of bound VHH molecules, respectively. Each dot indicates one particle. (i) Histogram overlay showing the distribution of functional VHH surface densities (molecules/100 nm2) across input groups. (j) Correlation between the input VHH mol % and median surface ligand density per particle (mean ± s.d., n = 3).

Figure caption: (a) In vivo delivery efficiency of CL4F8-6-based VHH-LNPs with varying ligand densities. Humanized mice were injected intravenously with mCherry mRNA-loaded LNPs (0.4 mg/kg), and mCherry expression in splenic CD8+ T cells was measured 24 h postinjection (mean ± s.d., n = 3 mice). (b) Representative flow cytometry dot plots of splenic human T cells stained for CD4 and CD8. The buffer, intermediate-density (0.008 mol % VHH input), and high-density (0.500 mol % VHH input) VHH-LNP groups are shown. (c) Quantification of CD8 and CD4 surface expression in vivo. Values indicate the geometric mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) normalized to the buffer group. Mean ± s.d., n = 3. (d) In vitro mCherry expression in activated human CD8+ T cells 24 h after transfection with CL4F8-6 LNPs at different ligand densities at doses of 0.3 or 0.03 μg/mL. (e) Representative dot plots of CD4 and CD8 expression from in vitro-transfected cells. The buffer, intermediate-density (0.031 mol % VHH input), and high-density (0.500 mol % VHH input) VHH-LNP groups are shown. (f) In vitro quantification of surface CD8 or CD4 molecules in CD3+CD4– T cells or CD3+CD4+ T cells, respectively. The values indicate the geometric MFI quantification, normalized to the buffer group. Mean ± s.d., n = 3. (g) Time course of mCherry expression after transfection with buffer, unconjugated LNPs, and intermediate- or high-density LNPs (0.03 μg/mL). Intermediate- and high-ligand densities indicate 0.031 mol % and 0.500 mol % VHH input, respectively. Mean ± s.d., n = 3. (h and i) Kinetics of CD8 (h) or CD4 (i) surface expression in CD3+CD4– T cells or CD3+CD4+ T cells post-transfection. Relative expression levels were determined by geometric MFI and normalized to the pretreatment baseline (0 min = 1.0) for each group. Mean ± s.d., n = 3. (j) Western blot analysis of hCD8α protein in whole-cell lysates from hPBMCs 3 h after LNP treatment at a dose of 0.03 μg/mL. High-density VHH-LNPs reduced full-length CD8α and induced detectable degradation fragments. β-Actin was used as a loading control. Anti-hCD8α antibody recognizes the C-terminus of human CD8α. (k) Schematic model of ligand density effects on receptor availability and mRNA delivery.

Figure caption: (a) Schematic of the in vitro cytotoxicity assay. Activated human T cells were transfected with buffer control, mCherry, or CD19 CAR mRNA-loaded hCD8-LNPs (optimal VHH density) at a dose of 0.3 μg mRNA/mL and then were cocultured with Nalm6-GFP/Luc leukemia cells at the indicated effector-to-target (E:T) ratio. (b) Representative fluorescence images of Nalm6-GFP cells 72 h after coculture with in vitro-generated CAR-T cells. Scale bars, 200 μm. (c) Quantification of GFP fluorescence intensity every 6 h (mean ± s.d., n = 3). (d) Apoptosis in Nalm6 cells was evaluated by Annexin V staining 24 h after coculture with in vitro LNP-transfected T cells at a dose of 3 μg mRNA/mL (mean ± s.d., n = 3). (e) IFN-γ secretion measured by ELISA 72 h following coculture of Nalm6 cells with in vitro LNP-transfected T cells at doses of 0.3 or 3.0 μg mRNA/mL (mean ± s.d., n = 3). (f) Antigen specificity of CAR-T activation as indicated by IFN-γ secretion post-transfection of hCD8-LNPs at a dose of 3 μg mRNA/mL. (g) Experimental design for in vivo therapeutic efficacy study. (h) Bioluminescence imaging of leukemic burden. The color bar indicates radiance (p/sec/cm2/sr). On day 0, mice were randomized to normalize tumor size. (i) Quantification of the bioluminescence signal over time (mean ± s.d., n = 5).

Figure caption: (a) CAR expression in CD8+ T and CD4+ T cells measured 3 h after in vitro transfection with hCD8-LNPs or unconjugated LNPs to activated T cells from hPBMCs. (b and c) Flow cytometry analysis showing dose-dependent depletion of CD19+ B cells 48 h after in vitro coculture of human B cells from a healthy donor with in vitro-activated T cells transfected with hCD8-LNPs (b) or unconjugated LNPs (c). Statistical significance was evaluated using one-way (b and c) or two-way (a) ANOVA with Dunnett’s post hoc multiple comparisons versus the mCherry mRNA-treated group (***P ≤ 0.001, ****P ≤ 0.0001; ns = not significant, P > 0.05). (d) Quantification of in vivo CAR expression in CD8+ T cells at 4 h postinjection across multiple doses (mean ± s.d., n = 3). (e) Time-course analysis of B cell depletion following a single intravenous administration of hCD8-LNPs encapsulating CAR mRNA (0.1 mg/kg) in humanized mice. (f and g) Human CD19+CD20+ B cell composition in human CD45+ cells in the spleen (f) and bone marrow (g) measured 24 h after a single intravenous dose of CD19 CAR mRNA-loaded hCD8-LNPs. Statistical significance was evaluated using one-way (f and g) ANOVA with Dunnett’s post hoc multiple comparisons versus the buffer control group (**P ≤ 0.01, ***P ≤ 0.001, ****P ≤ 0.0001; ns = not significant, P > 0.05).
